name: Bathing in ash (bhasmasnāna)
method_summary: At each of the three junctures of the day the practitioner purifies himself, takes ash consecrated with the mantras and rubs it over the whole body while muttering, then enters the temple.

name: Lying in ash (bhasmaśayana)
method_summary: The practitioner sleeps and lies on ash.

name: Re-bathing in ash (anusnāna)
method_summary: Between the three ash-baths, after impurity from eating, sneezing, spitting, urinating or evacuating, he bathes again with ash, for purity and to show the sign.

name: Wearing the used garland (nirmālya)
method_summary: He wears flowers taken down from the image, to increase devotion and show the sign.

name: Dwelling in the temple (āyatanavāsa)
method_summary: The first-stage practitioner lives in a temple built by another, under his teacher, as one lives on a riverbank.

name: One garment or none
method_summary: He wears a single garment, or goes naked.

name: The six-limbed offering (upahāra)
method_summary: Kneeling south of the image after the ash-bath, the practitioner mutters, then laughs loudly again and again, sings and dances, makes the bull-like ḍuṇḍuṅ sound, prostrates and mutters, then reports the offering to the Lord, circumambulates and takes a closing bath.

warnings.text: Where worldly people are present, all this is to be done secretly.

notes: The Ratnaṭīkā classes muttering and prostration as mental, dance as bodily, and laughter, song and the ḍuṇḍuṅ sound as vocal.

name: Loud laughter as offering (hasita, aṭṭahāsa)
method_summary: Loud laughter ('a-ha-ha'), opening throat and lips, offered to the Lord while absorbed in meditation on Śiva.

name: Song as offering (gīta)
method_summary: Singing of the Lord's qualities and deeds, following the rules of music.

name: Dance as offering (nṛtta)
method_summary: Dance with gestures of hands and feet according to the Nāṭyaśāstra, offered together with song.

name: The bull-sound (ḍuṇḍuṅkāra / huḍukkāra)
method_summary: A holy sound like a bull's bellow produced by touching the tongue-tip to the palate, made as part of the offering.

name: Prostration as offering (namaskāra)
method_summary: Homage to the Lord within the offering, performed mentally according to the Ratnaṭīkā; self-offering is made with prostrations while repeating the five mantras.

name: Muttering the five brahma-mantras
method_summary: Muttering of the Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna mantras (the five purifiers) during the ash-bath, the offering and circumambulation; muttering the five alone is also a cause of merit.

name: Expiatory and yogic recitation of the Raudrī Gāyatrī
method_summary: After seeing urine or faeces or speaking with women or śūdras, he touches water, performs breath-control and mutters the Raudrī Gāyatrī or the Bahurūpī; in the third stage recitation of the chosen Gāyatrī is the ground from which yoga proceeds.

name: Circumambulation (pradakṣiṇa)
method_summary: Clockwise circling of the image while muttering, after the offering; one of the vows. The Sūtra adds that in Rudra's worship the counter-clockwise too is clockwise.

name: Self-offering to the Lord (atidāna)
method_summary: The 'supreme gift': giving oneself to the Lord, with prostrations while repeating the five mantras, instead of gifts of cows, land or gold.
signs_of_progress: non-return after reaching Rudra's proximity (as the text states the fruit)

name: Pāśupata initiation
method_summary: The teacher tests a brahmin, consecrates him in the forenoon before the southern image of Mahādeva with ash sanctified by the five mantras, and makes him hear the mantra; material, time, rite, image and teacher are the five factors.
prerequisites: brahmin male, tested by the teacher; freedom from debts (Kuśika's declaration)

name: Courting dishonour (avamāna, paribhava)
method_summary: Hiding his sign and learning, the ascetic goes among people behaving so as to be despised and reviled; he regards censure as no censure. The text states that his demerit then passes to his revilers and their merit to him.
signs_of_progress: being thought mad or sinful by people (the intended result)

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Feigned sleep and snoring (krāthana)
method_summary: While awake he acts as if asleep, making a snoring sound in the throat with the out-breath, so that people despise him.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Feigned trembling (spandana)
method_summary: He deliberately shakes his limbs as if struck by a wind-disorder.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Feigned limping (maṇṭana)
method_summary: He walks as if his foot were injured.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Feigned amorous gestures (śṛṅgāraṇa)
method_summary: Standing at a distance from a group of women, he looks at one young woman and makes signs of desire such as arranging his hair, so as to be called unchaste; the act is a pretence.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Senseless acts (avitatkaraṇa)
method_summary: He handles sticks, clods and the like as one who cannot tell pure from impure or fit from unfit, without breaking the restraints.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Senseless speech (avitadbhāṣaṇa)
method_summary: He utters meaningless, repetitive or contradictory words.

warnings.text: Undertaken only after knowledge has been gained, impurity reduced and the teacher's permission obtained; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints (non-harming, celibacy etc.).

name: Going about like a wretch (pretācaraṇa)
method_summary: He lives unwashed, dirt-smeared, with hair, beard and nails grown and without grooming, like a poor madman, so that the marks of caste and āśrama are cut off and dispassion grows.

name: Wandering alone like a madman
method_summary: Having closed the doors of the senses with the intellect, he wanders alone as if mad, taking discarded food; people call him mad and foolish. Kauṇḍinya: the madness is a feint to delude worldly examiners.

name: Keeping the vow hidden (gūḍhavrata)
method_summary: He keeps his knowledge, austerity, vow and mantras concealed.

name: Closing the doors of the senses with the intellect
method_summary: With the intellect he shuts all the doors (senses), so that outwardly their working seems deranged.

name: Dwelling in an empty house or cave
method_summary: In the stage of conquest he lives in an empty house or cave free from distraction, constantly with the god, senses conquered, studying and meditating.
duration: six months of constant yoga are named for the powers to arise (PS 5.12-13)
signs_of_progress: powers such as distant sight arise gradually

name: Meditation on Oṃ with fixation in the heart
method_summary: Self-controlled, after reciting the chosen Gāyatrī, he meditates on the syllable Oṃ and holds the mind fixed in the heart.

name: Constant remembrance of Rudra
method_summary: He always remembers Rudra and, cutting with the intellect the root of the net of causes of faults, fixes the whole mind on Rudra.

name: Dwelling in the cremation ground
method_summary: In the fourth stage he lives in the cremation ground, in the open or at the foot of a tree, not leaving it until the body falls, living on what comes unasked, practising remembrance.

name: The Pāśupata livelihoods
method_summary: Alms (first and third stages), discarded food (second), whatever comes (fourth); in the fifth there is none. Alms are gathered with purity, avoiding certain houses, and offered to Śiva before eating; he lives after the manner of cows and deer and is purified by water alone.

name: The Vedic Pāśupata vow of the Atharvaśiras
method_summary: A vow taken for life or a set term: after the virajā fire-offering the ash is taken and the limbs are touched and smeared with the Atharvaśiras formulae ('fire is ash ...'), the three lines are applied, and Śiva-yoga is practised at the three junctures.

equivalents.note: both are ash-observances named pāśupata; the Purāṇas distinguish this Vedic form from the non-Vedic Pāśupata scriptures

name: The great vow of the skull (mahāvrata, kapālavrata)
method_summary: Summary only: the ascetic lives as a skull-bearer - skull as begging-bowl, skull-topped staff, ash - in imitation of the Lord's penance; named 'beyond the world' for the Lākulas and the Kāpāla vow by opponents.

name: Wearing the six insignia (reported)
method_summary: As reported by Yāmuna and Rāmānuja: knowing and wearing six insignia (ear-ornament or necklace, rucaka, earrings, crest-jewel, ash, sacred thread) with skull and khaṭvāṅga, claimed to prevent rebirth.

name: Meditation on the self seated in the yoni (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: an opponent's one-line report that the Kāpālas attain nirvāṇa by meditating on the self as seated in the yoni. No further description is recorded here.
notes: Sexual rite category: restricted, summary only.

name: Skull-eating and corpse-ash practices (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas eat from a skull, bathe in the ash of corpses and eat it, and carry a club, as means to seen and unseen ends.

warnings.text: Yāmuna declares these acts forbidden by every scripture.

name: Worship of the deity in a pot of liquor (reported)
method_summary: Summary only: opponents report that the Kālāmukhas set up a pot of liquor and worship the deity placed in it.

name: Night rite in the great cremation ground (literary)
method_summary: Summary only: in Bāṇa's Harṣacarita the Śaiva adept Bhairavācārya performs a mantra-rite at night in the great cremation ground, guarded by the king and disciples.
notes: Named 'vetāla-sādhana' in scholarship; the text's details were not checked in this run.
